message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering credible vulnerability reports and material advisory updates observed from 2026-07-27 05:10 IST through 2026-07-28 05:10 IST. One relevant monitored-product update was confirmed: CISA added a Fortinet FortiOS vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 27, 2026.

**Finding 1**

- Product: Fortigate/FortiOS
- Issue: CVE-2025-68686, Fortinet FortiOS Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor Vulnerability
- Severity: Medium, based on Fortinet CNA CVSS 3.1 score 5.9. NVD had not provided its own CVSS assessment at the time reviewed.
- Description: NVD describes this as a FortiOS SSL-VPN sensitive-information exposure issue that may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch for a symbolic-link persistence mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases via crafted HTTP requests. The NVD record notes that an attacker would first need filesystem-level compromise through another vulnerability.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Fortigate/FortiOS, and the NVD record explicitly lists affected FortiOS versions. The fresh item is the July 27, 2026 CISA KEV update, which changed CISA's SSVC exploitation status to active and added the vulnerability to the KEV catalog.
- Source: NVD CVE-2025-68686 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-68686; CISA KEV reference via NVD https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?field_cve=CVE-2025-68686; Fortinet vendor advisory referenced by NVD https://fortiguard.fortinet.com/psirt/FG-IR-25-934

**Possible matches needing review**

No ambiguous MongoDB or product-family matches were strong enough to include. A Ubiquiti/UniFi RCE chain appeared in current aggregator coverage, but the Ubiquiti advisory was published in May 2026 and the CISA KEV addition was in June 2026, so it was excluded as stale for this 24-hour digest.

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for FortiOS deployments, especially internet-exposed SSL-VPN or previously compromised FortiOS assets, because CISA now lists CVE-2025-68686 as known exploited. No other confirmed new relevant vulnerabilities were verified for the monitored products in this run.
